newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's SBF confirms in talks with CME, Nymex.
newsitem.headline: France's SBF confirms in talks with CME, Nymex.

text.p: The French stockmarkets association SBF said on Monday it was in talks with the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) and New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) about a technology-sharing agreement.

An SBF spokesman confirmed the discussions when queried by Reuters about an article in the Financial Times which said the Paris, New York and Chicago futures exchanges were discussing an agreement that could give them common clearing and screen-trading software by 1998.
The newspaper said Nymex and CME were negotiating with the Paris bourse to adopt its NSC screen-trading system.
At the same time, it said, Nymex and CME were talking to Paris about adopting their trade processing software called Clearing 21.
Matif, the French options and futures exchange, is developing the NSC jointly with the SBF.
Matif and CME were partners in the GLOBEX screen-based futures trading system and were interested in pursuing their transatlantic cooperation, the newspaper said.

The GLOBEX automated matching system was developed by Reuters Holdings Plc, the CME and the MATIF. Reuters said last week that GLOBEX was not likely to continue beyond 1998 as the original partners develop their own systems.

The SBF spokesman said it was logical to bring Nymex into the talks as it was joint proprietor of the Clearing 21 software along with the CME and might also be interested in the NSC system for after-hours trading.
